, this shows that the map

X\times_{Z}Y\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{Z}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{Z}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]

is an effective epimorphism and we have the equivalences thanks to the proof of Lemma
4.1.16
:

\begin{split}C(p_{X}\times_{p_{Z}}p_{Y})^{n}\simeq&C(p_{Y})^{n}\times_{Y}^{s_{n}}\left(X\times_{Z}Y\right)\\
\simeq&C(p_{Z})^{n}\times_{Z}^{s_{n}}Z\times_{Z}\left(X\times_{Z}Y\right)\\
\simeq&C(p_{Z})^{n}\times_{Z}^{s_{n}}\left(X\times_{Z}Y\right)\\
\simeq&\mathscr{G}^{n}\times_{Z}^{s_{n}}\left(X\times_{Z}Y\right)\end{split}

Moreover we have a commutative diagram of Segal groupoids:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces C(p_{X}\times_{p_{Z}}p_{Y})^{\bullet}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces C(p_{Y})^{\bullet}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces C(p_{X})^{\bullet}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces C(p_{Z})^{\bullet}}

This makes
C(p_{X}\times_{p_{Z}}p_{Y})^{\bullet}
the groupoids given by the “pullback action”. And because the
p_{X}\times_{p_{Z}}p_{Y}
is an effective epimorphism, we get an equivalence:

\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{Z}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{Z}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\simeq\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X\times_{Z}Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X\times_{Z}Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X\times_{Z}Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X\times_{Z}Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]

∎

4.1.2.
Tangent and cotangent complexes of quotient stacks

To study
\mathscr{G}
-equivariant geometry is to study the quotient stacks. In particular, we would like to have a better understanding of quasi-coherent sheaves on such quotient and on their tangent and cotangent complexes.

A first remark we can make is that since
p
is an effective epimorphism, using
[
Lur09b
, Lemma 6.2.3.16.]
, the pullback along
p
is a conservative functor between the slice categories. In particular, this implies that the functor:

p^{*}:\mathbf{QC}\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\right)\to\mathbf{QC}(X)

is conservative.

Moreover, it turns out that
p^{*}\mathbb{T}{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}
is easy to compute. However, in order to describe it, we need to understand the notion of “tangent to a groupoid”
\mathscr{G}
.

In the case of a group, the tangent is simply
G\times\mathfrak{g}
, with
\mathfrak{g}
the Lie algebra associated to
G
. For a groupoid, the situation is more complicated, but we can produce a
Lie algebroid
associated to
\mathscr{G}
playing the same role as
\mathfrak{g}
. We will describe this in details with Construction
4.2.1
. For now it suffices to say that we can construct a Lie algebroid over
X
, when
X
satisfies Assumptions
3.2.2
, encoding the infinitesimal action of
\mathscr{G}
on
X
.

In fact for this section, we do not need the full Lie algebroid, but only the underlying anchored linear stack. Given a Segal groupoid
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
we will therefore consider the following anchored module associated to
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
:

\mathscr{L}:=\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}\overset{\rho}{\to}\mathbb{T}_{X}

Therefore, we can work in a more general context where
X
is a stack that admits a cotangent complex.

Proposition 4.1.20
.

Let
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
be a Segal groupoid over
X
. Then we have that:

p^{*}\mathbb{T}_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}=\mathscr{L}[1]\oplus^{\rho}\mathbb{T}_{X}

where
\rho:\mathscr{L}\to\mathbb{T}_{X}
is the anchor.

Proof.

By definition of
\mathscr{L}
, using the fiber sequence defining the relative tangent complex, we get:

p^{*}\mathbb{T}_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}\simeq\mathrm{cofib}(\rho:\mathscr{L}\to\mathbb{T}_{X})\simeq\mathbb{T}_{X}\oplus^{\rho}\mathscr{L}[1]

∎

Remark 4.1.21
.

Unfortunately, it is more difficult to compute the tangent complex
\mathbb{T}_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}
because quasi-coherent sheaves on
\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]
are not always easy to describe.

However, if
\mathscr{G}=X\times G
comes from a smooth action of an affine group acting on a derived Artin stack
X
, then we have an equivalence:

G-\mathbf{QC}(X)\simeq\mathbf{QC}\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]\right)

It sends a
G
-equivariant sheaf
\mathscr{F}\in\mathbf{QC}(X)
to the limit of the cosimplicial diagram
\mathscr{O}_{G^{\bullet}}\otimes\mathscr{F}
. The pullback functor
p^{*}
along the projection amounts to forgetting the
G
-action. More details are given in the proof of Proposition
4.1.22

Proposition 4.1.22
.

Under the identification and assumptions of Remark
4.1.21
, we have an equivalence of
G
-equivariant modules:

\mathbb{L}_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}\simeq\mathbb{L}_{X}\oplus^{\rho}\mathscr{O}_{X}\otimes\mathfrak{g}^{*}[-1]

where
\rho
is
G
-equivariant with
G
acting on
\mathbb{L}_{X}
by the cotangent action and on
\mathfrak{g}^{*}[-1]\otimes\mathscr{O}_{X}
by the coadjoint action.

Sketch of proof.

When
G
is affine, we have an equivalence:

G-\mathbf{QC}(X)\to\mathbf{QC}(X\times G^{\bullet})^{\mathrm{Cart}}

where the right hand side is the category of
Cartesian
cosimplicial presheaves (see
[
TV08
, Definition 1.2.12.1.]
). This equivalence sends
V\in\mathbf{QC}(X)
to the cosimplicial set
\mathscr{O}_{G^{\bullet}}\otimes_{\mathscr{O}_{X}}V
.

Moreover, there is an equivalence:

\lim:\mathbf{QC}(X\times G^{\bullet})^{\mathrm{Cart}}\to\mathbf{QC}\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]\right)

This works under the assumption that the cosimplicial diagram satisfies descent according to
[
TV08
, Definition 1.2.12.1]
which is the case when
G
acts smoothly on
X
a derived Artin stacks, in the sens that
X\times G
is a smooth groupoid (Definition
4.1.6
). This is because the functor
\mathbf{QC}
satisfies smooth descent (since it satisfies fpqc descent).

Moreover, the
G
-module
\mathbb{L}_{X}\oplus^{\rho^{*}}\mathscr{O}_{X}\otimes\mathfrak{g}^{*}[1]
is equivalent to the limit of the cosimplicial diagram of
G
-equivariant modules:

\lim(\mathbb{L}_{X}\oplus^{\rho^{*}}\mathscr{O}_{X}\otimes(\mathfrak{g}^{*})^{\oplus\bullet})

This is sent to the Cartesian cosimplicial diagram:

\lim(\mathscr{O}_{G^{\star}}\otimes(\mathbb{L}_{X}\oplus^{\rho^{*}}\mathscr{O}_{X}\otimes(\mathfrak{g}^{*})^{\oplus\bullet}))

Since this is the limit of a bicosimplicial diagram, it is computed by the diagonal and we get:

\mathscr{O}_{G^{\bullet}}\otimes(\mathbb{L}_{X}\oplus^{\rho^{*}}\mathscr{O}_{X}\otimes(\mathfrak{g}^{*})^{\oplus\bullet}))\simeq\mathbb{L}_{X\otimes G^{\bullet}}

Therefore taking the limit of this diagram recovers
\mathbb{L}_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}
.
∎

Corollary 4.1.23
.

If
G
if affine and acting smoothly on
X
an Artin stack, the action of
G
on
\mathbb{L}_{X}\oplus^{\rho^{*}}\mathscr{O}_{X}\otimes\mathfrak{g}^{*}[-1]
gives an action on its associated linear stack such that:

\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{4.73654pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathbb{A}_{X}(\mathbb{L}_{X}\oplus^{\rho^{*}}\mathscr{O}_{X}\otimes\mathfrak{g}^{*}[-1])}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{4.48654pt}{$\textstyle{\mathbb{A}_{X}(\mathbb{L}_{X}\oplus^{\rho^{*}}\mathscr{O}_{X}\otimes\mathfrak{g}^{*}[-1])}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.3943pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathbb{A}_{X}(\mathbb{L}_{X}\oplus^{\rho^{*}}\mathscr{O}_{X}\otimes\mathfrak{g}^{*}[-1])}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.64061pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathbb{A}_{X}(\mathbb{L}_{X}\oplus^{\rho^{*}}\mathscr{O}_{X}\otimes\mathfrak{g}^{*}[-1])}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]\simeq T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]

Proof.

We have a pullback diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{A}_{X}\left(p^{*}\mathbb{L}_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}\right)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p}

This is a pullback since this is the pullback of the linear stack
T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]
along
p
. Therefore from Proposition
1.2.17
, this pullback is the linear stack associated to
p^{*}\mathbb{L}_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}
.

We can then use Proposition
4.1.20
and Lemma
4.1.16
to show that
T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]
is a quotient of
\mathbb{A}_{X}(\mathbb{L}_{X}\oplus^{\rho^{*}}\mathscr{O}_{X}\otimes\mathfrak{g}^{*}[-1])
by an action of
G
.

We need to show that this is exactly the action described in Proposition
4.1.22
. We observe that if we take the associated linear stack to the Cartesian quasi-coherent sheaf we used in the proof of Proposition
4.1.22
, we get a
Cartesian simplicial stack
over
X\times G^{\bullet}
, and we have a commutative diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{QC}\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]\right)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{QC}(X\times G^{\bullet})^{\mathrm{Cart}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{dSt}_{/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left(\mathbf{sdSt}_{/X\times G^{\bullet}}\right)^{\mathrm{Cart}}}

The horizontal arrows are equivalences with left adjoint given by the colimit functor. Therefore
T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]
is both the linear stack associated with
\mathbb{L}_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}
and the colimit of the simplicial diagram:

T^{*}(X\times G^{\bullet})\simeq T^{*}X\times(\mathfrak{g}^{*})^{\times\bullet}\times G^{\bullet}\simeq\mathbb{A}_{X}\left(\mathbb{L}_{X}\oplus^{\rho^{*}}\mathscr{O}_{X}\otimes\mathfrak{g}^{*}[-1]\right)\times G^{\bullet}

where these equivalence are the linear version of the equivalences explained in the proof of Proposition
4.1.22
.

Therefore
T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]
is the quotient of:

\mathbb{A}_{X}\left(\mathbb{L}_{X}\oplus^{\rho^{*}}\mathscr{O}_{X}\otimes\mathfrak{g}^{*}[-1]\right)

by the natural action described in Proposition
4.1.22
.

By effectivity of the quotient, this is the only action (up to equivalence) of
G
on
\mathbb{A}_{X}\left(p^{*}\mathbb{L}_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}\right)
whose quotient is
T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]
.
∎

4.1.3.
Some symplectic structures on quotients by a group action

In this section, we discuss some element of the symplectic
G
-equivariant geometry for
G
a group acting smoothly on
X
a derived Artin stack.

Example 4.1.24
.

The Lie algebra
\mathfrak{g}
of an affine group
G
admits an adjoint and a coadjoint action:

G\times\mathfrak{g}\to\mathfrak{g}\ \qquad G\times\mathfrak{g}^{*}\to\mathfrak{g}^{*}

We can see these actions as the natural actions on
G
on the tangent and cotangent complexes of
\mathbf{B}G
(see Proposition
4.1.22
).

Lemma 4.1.25

(
[
AC21
, Example 1.6]
)
.

If
G
if an affine group, there is an equivalence:

T^{*}[n+1]\mathbf{B}G\simeq\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.67209pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.8854pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]

Proof.

Consider the following pullback:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\star}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T^{*}[n+1]\mathbf{B}G}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{B}G}

This is a pullback because this is a pullback of linear stacks (Lemma
1.2.18
) and therefore is the linear stack associated with
p^{*}\mathbb{L}_{\mathbf{B}G}[n+1]
given, thanks to Proposition
4.1.20
, by
\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]
. We have seen in Lemma
4.1.16
that it implies that
T^{*}[n+1]\mathbf{B}G
is equivalent to a quotient of the pullback,
\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]
by
G
. This quotient is the quotient by the coadjoint action thanks to Corollary
4.1.23
.
∎

Remark 4.1.26
.

T^{*}[n+1]\mathbf{B}G
, and thus
\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.67209pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.8854pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]
, is canonically
(n+1)
-shifted symplectic.

Proposition 4.1.27
.

The natural projection
\mathfrak{g}^{*}\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.69293pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.44293pt}{$\textstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.67209pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.8854pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]
is Lagrangian.

Moreover, the pullback of the symplectic form on
\mathfrak{g}^{*}
is zero on the nose and the Lagrangian structure can be chosen to be zero.

Proof.

Since the symplectic structure described in Remark
4.1.26
is the canonical symplectic structure on a shifted cotangent, there is a model where it is strict in the sens that
\omega
is equal to its underlying
2
-form.
The pullback of this
2
-form is given by the composition:

\mathbb{T}_{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}\to p^{*}\mathbb{T}_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.89883pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.64883pt}{$\textstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70331pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.31978pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}\overset{\omega^{\flat}}{\to}p^{*}\mathbb{L}_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.89883pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.64883pt}{$\textstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70331pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.31978pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}\to\mathbb{L}_{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}

Using Proposition
4.1.20
, we have that:

p^{*}\mathbb{T}_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.89883pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.64883pt}{$\textstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70331pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.31978pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}\oplus^{\rho}\mathscr{O}_{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}\otimes\mathfrak{g}[1]\simeq\mathscr{O}_{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}\otimes(\mathfrak{g}^{*}\oplus\mathfrak{g}[1])

Then our composition is given by:

\mathscr{O}_{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}\otimes\mathfrak{g}^{*}\to\mathscr{O}_{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}\otimes(\mathfrak{g}^{*}\oplus\mathfrak{g}[1])\overset{\mathrm{id}}{\to}\mathscr{O}_{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}\otimes(\mathfrak{g}^{*}\oplus\mathfrak{g}[1])\to\mathscr{O}_{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}\otimes\mathfrak{g}[1]

This composition is
strictly
zero and is both a homotopy and strict fiber sequence, which proves that the “zero homotopy” is a Lagrangian structure.
∎

Proposition 4.1.28
.

The zero map
\star\to\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]
induces a Lagrangian morphism:

\mathbf{B}G\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.67209pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.8854pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]

Moreover, the pullback of the symplectic form on
\mathbf{B}G
is zero on the nose and the Lagrangian structure can be chosen to be the zero isotropic structure.

Proof.

This is the map induced by the zero section
\mathbf{B}G\to T^{*}[n+1]\mathbf{B}G
using the equivalence of Lemma
4.1.25
. From Remark
2.1.14
, since the zero section on
T^{*}[n+1]\mathbf{B}G
is strictly closed, we can pick the closure terms to be zero, which corresponds to taking a Lagrangian structure given by the
0
isotropic structure on the zero section.
∎

Proposition 4.1.29
.

If
X
is Artin and
G
is affine, acting smoothly on
X
, we have a pullback:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{B}G}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.69293pt}{$\displaystyle{T^{*}X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.44293pt}{$\textstyle{T^{*}X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.67209pt}{$\scriptstyle{T^{*}X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.8854pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{T^{*}X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.69293pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.44293pt}{$\textstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.67209pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.8854pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}

where
G
acts on
T^{*}X
by the
cotangent action
97
97

97

For any
g\in G
, the action induces a morphism
\phi_{g}:X\to X
that induces a map
T^{*}X\to T^{*}X
by pulling-back along
\phi_{g}
. This induces an action
G\times T^{*}X\to T^{*}X
. This the action induced by the dual of the anchor of the action Lie algebroid
\mathbb{L}_{X}\to\mathscr{O}_{X}\otimes\mathfrak{g}^{*}[-1]
.
and
T^{*}X\to\mathfrak{g}^{*}
is the dual of the infinitesimal action.

Proof.

The first step is to notice that there is an equivalence:

T^{*}X\times_{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}\star\simeq\mathbb{A}_{X}\left(p^{*}\mathbb{L}_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}\right)

To see that, notice that we have a commutative diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T^{*}X\times_{\mathfrak{g}^{*}}\star}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\star}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T^{*}X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X\times\mathfrak{g}^{*}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathfrak{g}^{*}}

where all squares are Cartesian. The leftmost square is a pullback of linear maps between linear stacks . Therefore, from Lemma
1.2.18
, the pullback is the linear stack associated to the fiber:

\mathrm{fiber}\left(T^{*}X\to X\times\mathfrak{g}^{*}\right)

which is exactly
\mathbb{A}_{X}\left(p^{*}\mathbb{L}_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}\right)
.

Then taking the quotient of this equivalence by the natural action of
G
, the result becomes a consequence of Proposition
4.1.19
since we have a pullback of quotients by actions of
G
. Then we use Corollary
4.1.23
to identify the quotient of
\mathbb{A}_{X}\left(p^{*}\mathbb{L}_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]}\right)
by
G
with
T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]
.
∎

We will see in Section
4.3.1
, that the map
T^{*}X\to\mathfrak{g}^{*}
is a moment map and therefore the canonical symplectic structure on
T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]
coincides with the one obtained from the pullback viewed as a derived intersection of Lagrangian morphisms.

4.2.
\mathscr{L}
-Equivariant Symplectic Geometry

In this section, we adapt the results of Section
4.1
to “infinitesimal actions” of Lie algebroids and discuss the relationship between
\mathscr{G}
-equivariant and
\mathscr{L}
-equivariant geometry.

We start in Section
4.2.1
by exploring the relationship between Lie algebroids and groupoids, describing the “derivation” of a groupoid and the “integration” of a Lie algebroid.

Moreover, we will explain that in good situations, the infinitesimal quotients of Lie algebroids are the formal completions of the projections to the quotients by the groupoids integrating the Lie algebroids. This in particular explains the terminology “infinitesimal quotient” that we use.

Then we will see in Section
4.2.2
the definitions and basic properties of
\mathscr{L}
-equivariant geometry. This is very similar to Section
4.1.1
and in particular,
\mathscr{L}
-equivariant geometry is the geometry of the infinitesimal quotients by Lie algebroids and their infinitesimal actions.

Then Section
4.2.3
deals with the description of the tangent and cotangent complexes of infinitesimal quotients.

4.2.1.
Derivation and integration of Lie algebroids

In this section, we discuss the procedure of “derivation” that produces a Lie algebroid out of a Segal groupoid. We will then show that Lie algebroids always “integrates” to a
formal
Segal groupoid. This is the analogue of the Lie differentiation and integration between Lie groups and Lie algebras.

We then proceed to show that in good situations, the infinitesimal quotient of a Lie algebroid can be identified with the formal thickening given by the formal completion of the projection to the quotient stack associated to a Segal groupoid integrating the Lie algebroid:

\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]\simeq\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}

We start with the description of the derivation procedure. Take
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
a Segal groupoid over
X=\mathbf{Spec}(A)
satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
. We would like to define the Lie algebroid associated to
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
as the relative tangent:

\mathscr{L}:=\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}

together with the Lie algebroid structure obtained from Proposition
3.1.7
. However, to use this proposition, we need the quotient stack to be
formal
, which is not quite general enough for the integration procedure.

Indeed, typical examples of groupoids whose quotient stacks are formal are
smooth
groupoids
98
98

98

The quotient stack of a smooth Segal groupoid is
Artin
and therefore formal thanks to Example
1.3.5
.
(Definition
4.1.6
), and it is well known that Lie algebroids do not always integrate to smooth Segal groupoids (see
[
CF03
]
). In general, it does not even seem true that Lie algebroids integrate to Segal groupoids whose quotients are
formal
, but we will see that they integrate to
formal Segal groupoids
(Definition
4.1.6
).

Therefore we are interested in Segal groupoids that admit a formal completion (Construction
4.1.10
) in particular, Segal groupoids such that
\mathscr{G}^{n}
is formal for all
n\geq 0
.

Furthermore, the correspondences between Lie algebroids, formal moduli problems and groupoids in much better behaved in
pre-stacks
. Since we still want to obtain stacks and Segal groupoids in stacks, we need to consider Segal groupoids in stack that are obtained as the stackification of a Segal groupoid in pre-stacks (the Segal groupoid in pre-stacks being some additional data).

In what follows, the bases,
X
and
Y
, are always affine. They will interchangeably be viewed as stacks or pre-stacks and we will not make any difference in notation between when they are seen as stacks or pre-stacks.

Construction 4.2.1
.

Take
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
a Segal groupoid over
X=\mathbf{Spec}(A)
satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
. We assume that
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
is given by the stackification of a groupoid
\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}
in formal pre-stacks
99
99

99

In particular if
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
is already formal, then the assumption is satisfied with
\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}=j(\mathscr{G}^{\bullet})
(viewed as a pre-stack).
. Then we can construct a Lie algebroid as follows:

(1)

Take the formal completion of the groupoid
\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}
, denoted
\widehat{\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}}
(Construction
4.1.10
).

(2)

Use
[
GR20
, Theorem 2.3.2]
and the equivalence:

\mathscr{B}_{X}:\mathbf{fpGpd}\overset{\sim}{\to}\mathbf{Thick}^{\mathrm{pre}}(X)

where
\mathbf{fpGpd}
denotes the category of formal Segal groupoids over
X
in the category of pre-stacks. We get
\mathscr{B}_{X}(\widehat{\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}})\in\mathbf{Thick}^{\mathrm{pre}}(X)
, which is equivalent to the data of a formal moduli problem under
X
thanks to Theorem
1.3.22
.

(3)

We take the associated Lie algebroid using the equivalence of Theorem
3.2.1
:

\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}:=\widetilde{\mathbb{T}}_{X/\mathscr{B}_{X}(\widehat{\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}})}

This construction is clearly natural with respect to morphisms of groupoids
\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}\to(\mathscr{G}^{\prime})_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}
over a fixed base. Moreover we have:

\mathscr{B}_{X}(\widehat{\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}})\simeq\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}

Remark 4.2.2
.

This construction depends on the choice of
\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}
. When
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
is formal, we will by default consider that
\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}=j(\mathscr{G}^{\bullet})
where
j:\mathbf{dSt}\to\mathbf{dpSt}
is the inclusion of stacks in pre-stacks. Moreover since
j
preserves formal completions (Proposition
1.3.24
), we have that:

\widehat{\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}}\simeq j(\widehat{\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}})

Remark 4.2.3
.

This is a priori different from the classical differentiation of a groupoid (see for Example
[
Cal21
, Section 1.2.3]
). Classically, the Lie algebroid is obtained as a Lie algebroid structure on:

\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}:=e^{*}\mathbb{T}_{\mathscr{G}/X}^{s}

where
\mathbb{T}_{\mathscr{G}/X}^{s}
denotes the relative tangent along the source map
s
with anchor given by
t_{*}
. We will see in Lemma
4.2.4
that there is an equivalence of anchored linear stacks:

e^{*}\mathbb{T}_{\mathscr{G}^{1}/X}^{s}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}

We do not know whether it is an equivalence of Lie algebroids whenever the classical construction makes sense or not (i.e. if the Lie brackets coincide).

Lemma 4.2.4
.

Let
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
be any Segal groupoid over
X
with
X
any derived stack such that both
\mathscr{G}^{1}
and
X
admit a cotangent complex. Then we have an equivalence of anchored
A
-modules:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces e^{*}\mathbb{T}_{\mathscr{G}^{1}/X}^{s}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{T}_{X}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\rho}

where
\rho
denotes the following composition:

e^{*}\mathbb{T}_{\mathscr{G}^{1}/X}^{s}\to e^{*}\mathbb{T}_{\mathscr{G}^{1}}\overset{t_{*}}{\to}\mathbb{T}_{X}

Proof.

Consider the pullback square:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathscr{G}^{1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces t}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces s}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p}

Since this is a pullback, we have an equivalence in
\mathbf{QC}(\mathscr{G})
:

\mathbb{T}_{\mathscr{G}/X}^{s}\simeq t^{*}\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}

This equivalence is part of the commutative diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{T}_{\mathscr{G}^{1}/X}^{s}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces t^{*}\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{T}_{\mathscr{G}^{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces t^{*}\mathbb{T}_{X}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces t_{*}}

We then only have to pullback this last diagram along the unit
e
to show the result.
∎

Proposition 4.2.5
.

Let
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
be a Segal groupoid over
X
, with
X
a stack that satisfies Assumptions
3.2.2
. Assume that each
\mathscr{G}^{n}
is formal. Then there is an equivalence of
A
-modules:

\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}:=\mathbb{T}_{X/\mathscr{B}_{X}\left(j(\widehat{\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}})\right)}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}

Proof.

In
[
GR20
, Section 2.4]
, it is shown that there is a pullback diagram in
\mathbf{dpSt}^{\mathrm{afp}}
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces j(\widehat{\mathscr{G}^{1}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathscr{B}_{X}\left(j(\widehat{\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}})\right)}

This implies that:

\mathbb{T}_{X/\mathscr{B}_{X}\left(j(\widehat{\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}})\right)}\simeq e^{*}\mathbb{T}_{j(\widehat{\mathscr{G}^{1}})/X}^{s}\simeq e^{*}\mathbb{T}_{\widehat{\mathscr{G}^{1}}/X}^{s}

Note that since
\widehat{\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}}
and
X
are stack, taking their tangents in stacks or pre-stack is the same.
Moreover, from Lemma
1.3.20
, the map
\widehat{\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}}\to\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
is formally étale, and therefore we have:

e^{*}\mathbb{T}_{\widehat{\mathscr{G}^{1}}/X}^{s}\simeq e^{*}\mathbb{T}_{\mathscr{G}^{1}/X}^{s}

Finally, we can conclude using Lemma
4.2.4
.
∎

If fact the assumption that for each
n\geq 0
,
\mathscr{G}^{n}
is formal has very nice consequences on the properties of the associated Lie algebroid and its quotient.

Proposition 4.2.6
.

Take
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
a Segal groupoid over
X
with
X
satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
and such that for each
n\geq 0
,
\mathscr{G}^{n}
is a formal stack. Then we have an equivalence:

\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}:=\mathscr{B}_{X}\left(j(\widehat{\mathscr{G}})\right)\simeq j\left(\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}\right)

Proof.

We have an equivalence of formal groupoids in pre-stacks:

\begin{split}X\times_{j\left(\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}\right)}X\simeq&j\left(X\times_{\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}}X\right)\\
\simeq&j\left(X\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{0.85416pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-0.85416pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{DR}}}X_{\mathrm{DR}}}X\right)\\
\simeq&j\left(\left(X\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}X\right)\times_{X_{\mathrm{DR}}\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{0.85416pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-0.85416pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{DR}}}X_{\mathrm{DR}}}X_{\mathrm{DR}}\right)\\
\simeq&j\left(\mathscr{G}^{1}\times_{\mathscr{G}^{1}_{\mathrm{DR}}}X_{\mathrm{DR}}\right)\\
\simeq&j(\widehat{\mathscr{G}^{1}})\end{split}

This equivalence extends to the
n
-simplices:

\underbrace{X\times_{j\left(\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}\right)}\cdots\times_{j\left(\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}\right)}X}_{\mathrm{n-times}}\simeq j(\widehat{\mathscr{G}^{n}})

Therefore, since
\mathscr{B}_{X}
is the inverse of the functor sending
f:X\to Y
to
C(f)^{\bullet}
, we get an equivalence:

j\left(\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}\right)\simeq\mathscr{B}_{X}(j(\widehat{\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}}))

∎

Corollary 4.2.7
.

Take
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
a Segal groupoid over
X
with
X
satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
and such that for each
n\geq 0
,
\mathscr{G}^{n}
is a formal stack. Then we have the following:

(1)

We have an equivalence:

\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]\simeq\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}

(2)

We have equivalences of
A
-modules:

\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]}\simeq\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}

Moreover, these equivalences give these modules the Lie algebroid structure coming from the one on
\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}
.

Proof.

(1)

By definition we have:

\mathscr{B}_{X}\left(j(\widehat{\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}})\right)\simeq\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}

Using Proposition
4.2.6
and the stackification functor, we get:

\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]:=\mathrm{Stf}\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}\right)\simeq\mathrm{Stf}\left(j\left(\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}\right)\right)\simeq\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}

(2)

We have the following equivalences:

\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{X/\mathscr{B}_{X}\left(j(\widehat{\mathscr{G}})\right)}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{X/j\left(\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}\right)}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{X/\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathsc
