Moreover since the map
\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]
is formally étale, we get:

\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{X/\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]}

∎

Remark 4.2.8
.

This shows that if
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
a Segal groupoid over
X
with
X
satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
and
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
is a formal stack, then the formal completion of a quotient stack is equivalent to the infinitesimal quotient of
X
by the associated Lie algebroid. This explains why we call them “infinitesimal quotients”.

So far, picking
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{pre}}
in Construction
4.2.1
is not useful if we restrict to Segal groupoids such that
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
is formal, which covers a rather large class of examples. However, when we want to integrate a Lie algebroid, it is unclear whether we will get a Segal groupoid of that sort. We will see that the integration procedure actually produces a Segal groupoid in pre-stacks
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{pre}}
.

We now turn toward the integration procedure.

Definition 4.2.9
.

Given a Lie algebroid
\mathscr{L}
over
X
with
X
satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
. We say that a Segal groupoid
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
over
X

integrates

\mathscr{L}
if
\mathscr{L}
is equivalent (as Lie algebroids) to
\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}
, the Lie algebroid associated to
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
.

Remark 4.2.10
.

Note that it is hopeless to have an integration procedure such that for all Segal groupoid
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
over
X
,
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
is the integration of its associated Lie algebroid
\mathscr{L}
since this property fails even for groups and Lie algebras. However, we can hope in good situations to recover the formal completion,
\widehat{\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}}
, of the groupoid we started with.

We are now going to prove a version of Lie’s third theorem, stating that every Lie algebroid ( over a base satisfying some assumptions) admits a formal integration.

Proposition 4.2.11
.

Take
\mathscr{L}
a Lie algebroid over
X
with
X
satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
. Consider the infinitesimal projection:

h:X\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]

We define the Segal groupoid:

\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}^{\bullet}:=C(h)^{\bullet}\simeq\underbrace{X\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}\cdots\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}X}_{\mathrm{\bullet-times}}

Then
\mathscr{L}
is the Lie algebroid associated to
\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}^{\bullet}
, obtained from Construction
4.2.1
using the Segal groupoid in pre-stacks given by:

(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}:=C(h_{\mathrm{pre}})^{\bullet}\simeq\underbrace{X\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}}\cdots\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}}X}_{\mathrm{\bullet-times}}

with

h_{\mathrm{pre}}:X\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}

Proof.

First, we want ot show that
(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}
is a formal Segal groupoid whose stackification in
\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}^{\bullet}
. Clearly,
X
and
(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}
are formal stacks. Moreover, the projection:

p:X\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}

is a nil-equivalence and this implies that all the structure morphisms of the Segal groupoid are nil-equivalences, making
\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}^{\bullet}
a formal Segal groupoid. Moreover since the stackification functor preserves pullbacks, we have:

\mathrm{Stf}((\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet})\simeq\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}^{\bullet}

We clearly have an equivalence:

\mathscr{B}_{X}((\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet})\simeq\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}

since
\mathscr{B}_{X}
is the inverse of the functor sending a formal thickening
f:X\to Y
to the formal Segal groupoid given by
C(f)
. Then under Assumptions
3.2.2
, the Lie algebroid associated to
\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]
is
\mathscr{L}
itself (using the Segal groupoid in pre-stack
(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}
).
∎

This proves that any Lie algebroid over
X
satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
can be
integrated
to a
formal
Segal groupoid (in our case
\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}^{\bullet}
). Moreover this defines a functor (over a fixed base) that sends
\mathscr{L}
to
\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}^{\bullet}
.

Remark 4.2.12
.

The Segal groupoid we produce,
\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}^{\bullet}
, is
not
smooth and it is well known that Lie algebroids
do not
always integrate to a smooth groupoids (see
[
CF03
]
). In general,
\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}
is instead the stackification of a formal groupoid in formal pre-stacks.
It is worth noting that the natural projections:

X\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}}$}}}\right]\qquad X\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.75pt}{$\textstyle{(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.625pt}{$\scriptstyle{(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}}$}}}\right]

are nil-equivalences. However, they are
not
formal thickenings as the quotients need not be formal (pre)-stacks.

One of the main drawback in having to use these pre-stacks is that the relative tangent of the infinitesimal quotient stack does not recover the Lie algebroid
100
100

100

This is essentially because the stackification functor does not preserve the tangent complexes
.

However, we have seen earlier that if
\mathscr{L}
is a Lie algebroid associated with a good class of Segal groupoid, then the relative tangent of the infinitesimal quotient stack is equivalent to
\mathscr{L}
. This motivates the following definition:

Definition 4.2.13
.

A Lie algebroids
\mathscr{L}
over
X
an affine stack satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
. Then
\mathscr{L}
is said to
integrate well
if there exists a Segal groupoid
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
such that for each
n\geq 0
,
\mathscr{G}^{n}
is a formal stack and such that
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
integrates
\mathscr{L}
, in other words, there is an equivalence of Lie algebroids:

\mathscr{L}\simeq\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}

Such a
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
will be called a
good integration
of
\mathscr{L}
. If
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
is smooth, it is called a
smooth integration
of
\mathscr{L}
.

Lemma 4.2.14
.

Let
\mathscr{L}
be a Lie algebroid over
X
an affine stack satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
that integrates well. Then there is an equivalence:

\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}\simeq\mathscr{L}

Proof.

Pick
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
a good integration of
\mathscr{L}
. Then thanks to Corollary
4.2.7
and the fact that
\mathscr{L}\simeq\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}
, we have the equivalences:

\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]}\simeq\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}\simeq\mathscr{L}

∎

Proposition 4.2.15
.

Let
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
be a Segal groupoid over
X
an affine stack satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
. We assume that
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}=\mathrm{Stf}\left(\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}\right)
and consider
\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}
the Lie algebroid obtained from Construction
4.2.1
using
\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}
. Then there is an equivalence of Segal groupoids:

\mathrm{Stf}\left(\widehat{\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}}\right)\simeq\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}^{\bullet}

Proof.

We have by definition that:

\mathscr{B}_{X}(\widehat{\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}})\simeq\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}

Therefore we get:

\widehat{\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}}\simeq C\left(X\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}\right):=(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}})^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{pre}}

Using the stackification functor, we get:

\mathrm{Stf}\left(\widehat{\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}}\right)\simeq\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}^{\bullet}

∎

Remark 4.2.16
.

In particular, if for each
n\geq 0
,
\mathscr{G}^{n}
is a formal stack, then
\mathscr{G}_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}=j(\mathscr{G}^{\bullet})
and since
j
commutes with the formal completion we get:

\widehat{\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}}\simeq\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}^{\bullet}

Therefore the integration of the groupoid associated to
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
is
not

\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
itself, but rather its formal completion.

We now turn to the behavior of the differentiation and integration constructions with respect to actions of Lie algebroids and Segal groupoids. First we are going to look at actions on
f:Y\to X
, a map of stacks satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
.

This differentiation procedure behaves well with respect to
actions
in the sens that any action on
f:Y\to X
of a Segal groupoid
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
such that for each
n\geq 0
,
\mathscr{G}^{n}
is a formal stack, induces an infinitesimal action of its associated Lie algebroid
\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}
on
f
.

Proposition 4.2.17
.

Let
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
be a Segal groupoid over
X
such that
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
is a formal stack and for each
n\geq 0
,
\mathscr{G}^{n}
is a formal stack. Then consider an action of
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
on
f:Y\to X
and suppose that both
X
and
Y
satisfy Assumptions
3.2.2
. Then this induces an action of
\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}
on
f
, and this defines a functor:

\mathbf{Act}_{\mathscr{G}}\to\mathbf{Act}_{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}

Proof.

is a formal thickening.

Since
f^{*}\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}=\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}\times_{X}^{s_{\bullet}}Y
also satisfies that each

is formal, and its quotient stack is
\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]
, then
\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{Y}}
is equivalent to the quotient of

by the Lie algebroid associated to

(again thanks to Corollary
4.2.7
).

Looking at the relative tangent of these pullbacks and using Corollary
4.2.7
, we get the equivalences:

\mathbb{T}_{Y/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{Y/\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{Y}}}\overset{\sim}{\to}f^{*}\mathbb{T}_{Y/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}\simeq f^{*}\mathscr{L}

This gives
f^{*}\mathscr{L}
the structure of a Lie algebroid.

We want to find a morphism of Lie algebroids
f^{*}\mathscr{L}\to\mathscr{L}
. To do that, notice that we have a pullback diagram (because
j
preserves pullbacks):

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces j\left(\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{Y}}\right)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces j\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]\right)}

From Proposition
4.2.6
we have the equivalences:

\mathscr{B}_{X}\left(j(\widehat{f^{*}\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}})\right)\simeq j\left(\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{Y}}\right)\qquad\mathscr{B}_{X}\left(j(\widehat{\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}})\right)\simeq j\left(\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}\right)

Therefore these are all formal pre-stacks and we can use Proposition
3.2.33
which shows that:

\mathbb{T}_{Y/j\left(\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{Y}}\right)}\to\mathbb{T}_{X/j\left(\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}\right)}

is a morphism of Lie algebroids.

Then we get a morphism of Lie algebroid:

f^{*}\mathscr{L}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{Y/\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{Y}}}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{Y/j\left(\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{Y}}\right)}\to\mathbb{T}_{X/j\left(\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}\right)}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{X/\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}}\simeq\mathscr{L}

∎

Proposition 4.2.18
.

Let
f:Y\to X
be a morphism of affine stacks satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
. Let
\mathscr{L}
be a Lie algebroid on
X
with an action on
f
. Then this induces an action of the formal groupoid integrating
\mathscr{L}
on
f
defining a functor:

\mathbf{Act}_{\mathscr{L}}\to\mathbf{Act}_{\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}}

Proof.

Given an action of
\mathscr{L}
on
f:Y\to X
, we first need to prove this statement for the pre-stacks. We first show that the following commutative diagram in pre-stacks is a pullback
101
101

101

We will show in Proposition
4.2.25
that a map of Lie algebroid induces such a commutative diagram.
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}}

Denote by
P
the pullback, and
\phi:Y\to P
the natural morphism.
P
and
Y
are formal and
\phi
is a nil-equivalence because:

P_{\mathrm{DR}}\simeq\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}\right)_{\mathrm{DR}}\overset{\sim}{\leftarrow}Y_{\mathrm{DR}}

Moreover we have a fiber sequence:

\mathbb{T}_{Y/P}\to\mathbb{T}_{Y/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}}\to\phi^{*}\mathbb{T}_{P/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}}\simeq f^{*}\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}}

The second morphism is clearly an equivalence as both complexes are equivalent to
\phi^{*}\mathscr{L}
and therefore
\phi
is formally étale. This proves that
\phi
is an equivalence thanks to Lemma
1.3.21
.

Now we have the following equivalences:

\begin{split}(\mathscr{G}_{f^{*}\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}^{1}\simeq&Y\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}}Y\\
\simeq&X\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}}Y\\
\simeq&X\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}}Y\\
\simeq&\left(X\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}}X\right)\times_{X}Y\\
\simeq&(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}})^{1}_{\mathrm{pre}}\times_{X}^{s}Y\\
\simeq&f^{*}(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}})^{1}_{\mathrm{pre}}\end{split}

Moreover, by induction, we get that:

\begin{split}(\mathscr{G}_{f^{*}\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}^{n}\simeq&(\mathscr{G}_{f^{*}\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}^{n-1}\times_{Y}(\mathscr{G}_{f^{*}\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}^{1}\\
\simeq&f^{*}\left(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}\right)_{\mathrm{pre}}^{n-1}\times_{Y}(\mathscr{G}_{f^{*}\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}^{1}\\
\simeq&f^{*}\left(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}\right)_{\mathrm{pre}}^{n-1}\times_{Y}Y\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}}Y\\
\simeq&f^{*}\left(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}\right)_{\mathrm{pre}}^{n-1}\times_{Y}f^{*}(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}})^{1}_{\mathrm{pre}}\\
\simeq&f^{*}\left(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}}\right)_{\mathrm{pre}}^{n}\end{split}

Therefore the Segal groupoid integrating
f^{*}\mathscr{L}
is equivalent to a Segal groupoid structure on
(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}\times_{X}^{s_{\bullet}}Y
. Moreover, since there is a natural morphism of groupoids
(\mathscr{G}_{f^{*}\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}\to(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}
over
f
, this defines an action of
(\mathscr{G}_{\mathscr{L}})_{\mathrm{pre}}^{\bullet}
on
f
.

Then the statement is the stackification of this construction.
∎

The main issue we will have is that all of this only works if
X
and
Y
satisfy Assumptions
3.2.2
which is too strict for most examples we will be interested in (e.g. the derived critical locus, zero loci of moment maps etc…).

We need to come up with a weakened notion of infinitesimal quotient. We actually only need this for infinitesimal quotients of actions on
f:Y\to X
where
X
satisfies Assumptions
3.2.2
and
Y
is affine of almost finite presentation.

Definition 4.2.19
.

Let
f:Y\to X
be a morphism of stack with
X
satisfying Assumptions

and

affine of almost finite presentation. Take

. Then a

of

by

is a derived stack, denoted by

, that fits in the pullback diagram:

Remark 4.2.20
.

This notion does not really use an action of
\mathscr{L}
. Therefore, even if
\mathscr{L}
does not act on
f
in the sens of Definition
3.3.12
, this defines a notion of weak infinitesimal quotient.

Note that this does not even depend on the Lie algebroid structure on
X
but only on its infinitesimal projection:

h:X\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]

Remark 4.2.21
.

Since this construction only depends on the infinitesimal quotient projection, we can also define a weak infinitesimal quotient
compatible
with a weak infinitesimal quotient
\widetilde{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}
along a morphism
Y^{\prime}\to Y
as a derived stack
\widetilde{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{4.00891pt}{$\displaystyle{Y^{\prime}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.75891pt}{$\textstyle{Y^{\prime}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.8978pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y^{\prime}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.11111pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y^{\prime}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}
fitting in a pullback diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y^{\prime}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widetilde{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{4.00891pt}{$\displaystyle{Y^{\prime}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.75891pt}{$\textstyle{Y^{\prime}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.8978pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y^{\prime}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.11111pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y^{\prime}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widetilde{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}}

In particular it is also automatically a weak infinitesimal quotient of
\mathscr{L}
along the composition:

Y^{\prime}\to Y\to X

One of the main difficulty when dealing with (weak) infinitesimal quotients of Lie algebroids is that we do not know whether there is an equivalence:

\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}\simeq\mathscr{L}

However, we have seen in Lemma
4.2.14
that if
\mathscr{L}

integrates well
(in the sens of Definition
4.2.13
), then the relative tangent recovers
\mathscr{L}
.

Corollary 4.2.22
.

Let
{\widetilde{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}}
be a weak infinitesimal quotient of
f:Y\to X
as before. Assume that
\mathscr{L}
integrates well. Then using the pullback defining
{\widetilde{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}}
and Lemma
4.2.14
, we get an equivalence in
\mathbf{QC}(Y)
:

\mathbb{T}_{Y/{\widetilde{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}}}\simeq f^{*}\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}\simeq f^{*}\mathscr{L}

This Corollary does not give a Lie algebroids structure on
f^{*}\mathscr{L}
since
Y
does not need to satisfy Assumptions
3.2.2
. Therefore we cannot recover an action of
\mathscr{L}
as in Proposition
4.2.17
.

Clearly, if
Y
satisfy Assumptions
3.2.2
and
\mathscr{L}
has an action on
Y\to X
, then
\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]
is a valid choice of weak infinitesimal quotient (but not necessarily the only one even up to equivalence).

Example 4.2.23
.

The Lie algebroid associated with a smooth action of an affine group
G
on
X
(with
X
satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
) is exactly the
action Lie algebroid
of Example
3.1.8
.

To see that, observe that
G
is naturally a groupoid over the point
\star
with Lie algebroid given by the Lie algebra
\mathfrak{g}
associated to
G
. Then a smooth action of
G
on
X
is exactly a smooth action as in Proposition
4.2.17
. Therefore the Lie algebroid associated with the action groupoid
G\times X
is
f^{*}\mathfrak{g}=X\times\mathfrak{g}
. Since the morphism
X\times\mathfrak{g}\to\mathfrak{g}
must be a morphism of Lie algebroids, this implies that the Lie bracket on
X\times\mathfrak{g}
is exactly the Lie bracket described in Example
3.1.8
.

4.2.2.
\mathscr{L}
-equivariant maps and (weak) infinitesimal quotients

This section is about having an analogue to Section
4.1.1
for infinitesimal action.
We start by defining the notion of
\mathscr{L}
-equivariant map by analogy to Definition
4.1.12
.

Definition 4.2.24
.

Let
f:X\to Y
be a morphism of derived stacks. Assume that
\mathscr{L}
is a Lie algebroid over
X
, a stack satisfying Assumptions

. Then the structure of an
invariant map with respect to
\mathscr{L}
on

is a factorization through the ‘‘projection’’
102
102

102

We still call the natural formal thickening:

a “projection” by analogy with the groupoid case. But it needs not be an effective epimorphism.

These notion of invariance and equivariance also make sens in pre-stacks by replacing all the infinitesimal quotient by the pre-stacks they are coming from.

In Section
4.1.1
, any morphism between quotient stacks would come from a morphism between Segal groupoids thanks to Lemma
4.1.11
. The infinitesimal projections are no longer effective epimorphisms in general but we still have the following:

Proposition 4.2.25
.

Take map
f:Y\to X
of finitely presented affine stacks satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
and
\mathscr{L}^{\prime}
and
\mathscr{L}
, Lie algebroids over
Y
and
X
respectively. Then we have that:

–

A morphism of Lie algebroids
\mathscr{L}^{\prime}\to\mathscr{L}
over
f:Y\to X
induces an equivariant map
\left[f\right]
. Moreover, it is obtained as the stackification of an equivariant map in pre-stacks:

\left[f\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}:\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-4.00891pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.75891pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.8978pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.11111pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}

–

Given an equivariant map
\left[f\right]
, if it comes from the stackification of an equivariant map in pre-stacks
\left[f\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}
, then there is a map,
\mathscr{L}^{\prime}\to\mathscr{L}
, of Lie algebroids over
f
.

–

Given an equivariant map
\left[f\right]
, if
\mathscr{L}^{\prime}
and
\mathscr{L}
integrate well in the sens of Definition
4.2.13
, then there is a morphism of Lie algebroids
\mathscr{L}^{\prime}\to\mathscr{L}
over
f
.

Proof.

If we have a morphism of Lie algebroids

over

, then by definition it factors as:

\mathscr{L}^{\prime}\to f^{!}\mathscr{L}\to\mathscr{L}

3.2.30
we have a commutative diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}}

We have this factorization because the formal completion is equivalent to the fiber product:

\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}\times_{\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}\right)_{\mathrm{DR}}}Y_{\mathrm{DR}}\simeq\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}\times_{\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}\right)_{\mathrm{DR}}}\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-4.00891pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.75891pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.8978pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.11111pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}\right)_{\mathrm{DR}}

and therefore receives a natural morphism from
\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-4.00891pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.75891pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.8978pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.11111pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}
.

The square is induced by the natural morphism of Lie algebroids
f^{!}\mathscr{L}\to\mathscr{L}
over
f
and the commutative triangle on the left induces (by naturality over a fixed base) a morphism of Lie algebroids
\mathscr{L}^{\prime}\to f^{!}\mathscr{L}
, which is exactly the data of a morphism of Lie algebroids
\mathscr{L}^{\prime}\to\mathscr{L}
over
f
.

For the last statement, observe that under the assumptions on
\mathscr{L}^{\prime}
and
\mathscr{L}
, we can take:

\left[f\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}:=j(\left[f\right]):\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-4.00891pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.75891pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.8978pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.11111pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}\simeq j\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-4.00891pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.75891pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.8978pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.11111pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}$}}}\right]\right)\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}\simeq j\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]\right)

and use the previous result.
∎

Proposition 4.2.26
.

Let
X
and
Y
be stacks satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
and
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
a Segal groupoid over
X
that is a good integration of a Lie algebroid
\mathscr{L}
. Then we have an equivalence of Lie algebroids:

f^{!}\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}\simeq\mathscr{L}_{f^{!}\mathscr{G}}

Proof.

It is enough to show that the associated formal groupoids in pre-stacks are equivalent. The formal groupoid in pre-stacks associated to
f^{!}\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}
is the formal completion:

Y\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.46028pt}{$\displaystyle{f^{!}\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.21028pt}{$\textstyle{f^{!}\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.10435pt}{$\scriptstyle{f^{!}\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.72083pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{f^{!}\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}}Y\simeq Y\times_{\widehat{\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}\right)_{Y}}}Y

Or the other side, the formal groupoid associated to
\mathscr{L}_{f^{!}\mathscr{G}}
is the groupoid given by:

\widehat{\left(Y\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}Y\right)}\simeq Y\times_{\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{Y}}}Y

We can then conclude by using the equivalences:

\begin{split}\widehat{\left(Y\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}}Y\right)}\simeq&\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{DR}}}X_{\mathrm{DR}}\times_{X_{\mathrm{DR}}}Y_{\mathrm{DR}}\\
\simeq&\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}\times_{X_{\mathrm{DR}}}Y_{\mathrm{DR}}\\
\simeq&\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}\times_{\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}\right)_{\mathrm{DR}}}Y_{\mathrm{DR}}\\
\simeq&\widehat{\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}_{\mathscr{G}}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{pre}}\right)_{Y}}\end{split}

∎

It turns out that pullbacks of an infinitesimal quotient projection are themselves infinitesimal quotient given by an infinitesimal action (by analogy with Lemma
4.1.16
).

Lemma 4.2.27
.

Let
X
be a stack satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
,
Z
a formal stack and
\mathscr{L}
a Lie algebroid on
X
that integrates well. Consider the following pullback diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}

Assume that
Y
also satisfies Assumptions
3.2.2
. Then we have the following:

(1)

Y\to Z
is a formal thickening and therefore is equivalent to the data of a formal moduli problem
F
.

(2)

There is an equivalence in
\mathbf{QC}(Y)
:

\mathbb{T}_{Y/Z}\overset{\sim}{\to}f^{*}\mathscr{L}

giving
f^{*}\mathscr{L}
a structure of Lie algebroid.

(3)

There is an infinitesimal action of
\mathscr{L}
on
Y\to X
such that:

Z\simeq\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]

Proof.

(1)

Applying
(-)_{\mathrm{DR}}
(which is a right adjoint) we have that the morphism:

Y_{\mathrm{DR}}\to Z_{\mathrm{DR}}

is the pullback morphism of the equivalence:

X_{\mathrm{DR}}\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]_{\mathrm{DR}}

Therefore
Y\to Z
is a formal thickening (since both
Y
and
Z
are formal). Since
Y
satisfies Assumptions
3.2.2
, Theorem
1.3.22
implies that
Z
is equivalent to the extension of a formal moduli problem under
Y
,
F
.

(2)

The relative cotangent of these formal thickenings are equivalent (because of the pullback) and thanks to Lemma
4.2.14
(with our assumption that
\mathscr{L}
integrates well), we have:

\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}\simeq\mathscr{L}

Therefore
f^{*}\mathscr{L}
has a structure of Lie algebroid given by the Lie algebroid structure on the relative cotangent
\mathbb{T}_{Y/F}
. Here we use the equivalences:

\mathbb{T}_{Y/F}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{Y/\underline{F}_{\mathrm{pre}}}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{Y/j(Z)}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{Y/Z}\simeq f^{*}\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}\simeq f^{*}\mathscr{L}

using Lemma
1.3.27
, Proposition
1.3.14
and Lemma
4.2.14
.

(3)

Proposition
3.2.33
gives us a morphism of Lie algebroids:

f^{*}\mathscr{L}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{Y/Z}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{Y/j(Z)}\to\mathbb{T}_{X/j\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]\right)}\simeq\mathbb{T}_{X/\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}\simeq\mathscr{L}

This is exactly the data of an action of
\mathscr{L}
on
Y\to X
such that there is an equivalence of Lie algebroids:

f^{*}\mathscr{L}\simeq\widetilde{\mathbb{T}}_{Y/F}

Therefore there is an equivalence:

\MC_{f^{*}\mathscr{L}}\simeq F

This implies that
f^{*}\mathscr{L}
is a Lie algebroid on
Y
whose infinitesimal quotient is:

Z\simeq\underline{F}\simeq\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]

∎

Remark 4.2.28
.

If we only assume that
Y
is affine and almost finitely presented, and if
Z
can be any derived stack, then
Z
is by definition a
weak
infinitesimal quotient of
Y
by
\mathscr{L}
. This makes the “weak analogue” of Lemma
4.2.27
tautological. More precisely we get:

–

The morphism
Y\to Z
is a nil-equivalence.

–

If
\mathscr{L}
integrates well then from Lemma
4.2.14
, there is an equivalence:

\mathbb{T}_{Y/Z}\overset{\sim}{\to}f^{*}\mathscr{L}

–

For any
\mathscr{L}
(even if it does not integrate well),
Z
is a weak infinitesimal quotient along:

Z:=\widetilde{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}

.

It is enough to show that we have a pullback diagram:

We will now turn to pullbacks of infinitesimal quotient stacks of Lie algebroids. First recall that any action of the Lie algebroid
\mathscr{L}
over
f:X\to Y
induces a map between their infinitesimal quotient stacks thanks to Proposition

:

\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Y}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]

We want show by analogy to Proposition
4.1.19
that the fiber product of the infinitesimal quotient stacks is the infinitesimal quotient stack associated to the fiber product of the Lie algebroids.

In practice, this would requires us to assume that
X
,
Y
,
Z
and

all satisfy Assumptions
3.2.2
which is very restrictive
103
103

103

In particular the fiber product of stacks satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
does not necessarily satisfy Assumptions
3.2.2
.
. Therefore we will only make an analogue for
weak
infinitesimal quotients.

We already know from Lemma
