. Under Assumptions
3.2.2
, we have seen that:

p^{*}\mathbb{L}_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}\simeq\mathbb{L}_{X}\oplus^{\rho}\mathscr{L}^{\vee}[-1]

∎

Proposition 4.2.34
.

Assume that
\mathbb{L}_{A}
is non-negatively graded and almost finitely presented, and that
\mathscr{L}
is almost finitely presented, concentrated in non-positive degrees and integrates well. Then
T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]
is a weak infinitesimal quotient of
\mathbb{A}_{X}(\mathbb{L}_{A}\oplus^{\rho}\mathscr{L}^{\vee}[-1])
.

Proof.

The assumptions ensure that
\mathbb{A}_{X}(\mathbb{L}_{A}\oplus^{\rho}\mathscr{L}^{\vee}[-1])
is affine of almost finite presentation. Then Proposition
4.2.33
shows that
T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]
is a weak infinitesimal quotient of
\mathbb{A}_{X}(\mathbb{L}_{A}\oplus^{\rho}\mathscr{L}^{\vee}[-1])
according to Definition
4.2.19
.
∎

4.3.
Shifted Moment Maps and Derived Symplectic Reduction

In this section, we develop the notion of
moment maps
for Lie algebroids and Segal groupoids. The main motivation is to define
symplectic reduction
in these contexts.

We start in Section
4.3.1
by recalling the classical notion of moment map and symplectic reduction for group actions in the context of derived algebraic geometry as developed in
[
AC21
]
. We recall the main important properties of these objects, notably the fact that they behave well under “good Lagrangian intersections” (Theorem
4.3.10
).

Then in Section
4.3.2
we generalize these notion and define the notion of
infinitesimal moment map
for the infinitesimal action of a Lie algebroid. We show that this definition naturally contains the notion of
infinitesimal symplectic reduction
and that it is also well behave with respect to “good Lagrangian intersections”.

Finally, we will explain in Section
4.3.3
that the notion of infinitesimal moment maps and infinitesimal symplectic reduction transfers directly to a notion of moment map and symplectic reduction for Segal groupoids by mimicking the definitions of Section
4.3.2
. Therefore moment maps and symplectic reductions also have the same properties.

The context of Segal groupoids is the most general and in particular, it recovers the case of moment maps for group actions (see Example
4.3.24
) and the example of the dual of the anchor of the associated Lie algebroid (Proposition
4.3.25
).

Moreover, we will see with Theorem
4.3.30
that in fact, the infinitesimal moment maps and infinitesimal symplectic reductions are in fact obtained via Construction
4.2.1
, Proposition
4.2.17
and formal completions, from moment maps and symplectic reductions of Segal groupoids. This follows the ideas of Section
4.2.1
making all the constructions for Lie algebroids the “infinitesimal versions” of the corresponding constructions for Segal groupoids.

4.3.1.
For groups

Let

be a smooth symplectic manifold and

104

Remark 4.3.3
.

In differential geometry, the conditions to be a moment map are
properties
of the map. As often in derived geometry, these properties become extra structures. Indeed, being equivariant is the
structure
of an equivariant map, as we have seen in Definition
4.1.1
and the second condition becomes the data of a Lagrangian
structure
. Therefore being a moment map will be a
structure
on the map
\mu
, and as often, we will keep saying that
\mu

is
a moment map to refer to
\mu
together with a structure of moment map.

We are interested in the procedure of symplectic reduction. Classically, it amounts (under the condition that these constructions exist) to do the following:

–

Take the zero locus

107

107

This can be generalized to taking the pre-image of any coadjoint orbit of

(see

). We are not going to consider this degree of generality.
of the moment map:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z(\mu)}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}

Remark 4.3.5
.

Taking this pullback took care of all 3 steps of the classical construction at once. Indeed, from Proposition
4.1.19
, this pullback is equivalent to:

\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X\times_{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}\star}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X\times_{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}\star}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X\times_{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}\star}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X\times_{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}\star}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]

Therefore
{X}_{\mathrm{red}}
is exactly the quotient of the fiber of
\mu
. And the symplectic structure comes for free from the fact that it is a derived intersection of Lagrangian morphisms (Propositions
4.3.1
and
4.1.28

Moreover, since the Lagrangian structure on
\mathbf{B}G\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{2.67209pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{G}$}}{\raisebox{1.8854pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{G}$}}}\right]
is the zero structure, and the Lagrangian structure on the moment map is given by the symplectic structure on
X
, the symplectic structure on
{X}_{\mathrm{red}}
is in some sens “induced” by the symplectic structure on
X
.

The following proposition is one of the main observation that will motivate the definition generalizing of the notion of moment map for Lie algebroids in Section
4.3.2
. Moreover Sections
4.3.2
and
5
will motivate the fact that these Lagrangian correspondences will be the defining feature of a generalized notion of symplectic reduction (Definitions

and

), viewed as a procedure to obtain symplectic stacks from quotients of “almost derived critical loci”.

Proposition 4.3.6

(
[
AC21
, Remark 2.4]
)
.

If
\mu:X\to\mathfrak{g}^{*}[n]
is a

4.3.2.

We want to generalize the definition of a moment map for infinitesimal actions of Lie algebroids. As we are working with Lie algebroids again, we will assume that

The goal is two-fold, we want to recover the infinitesimal counterpart of Section

Given a map

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{T}_{Z(\rho^{*})}}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{*}\mathbb{T}_{T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi^{*}\mathscr{L}}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces g^{*}\mathbb{T}_{T^{*}X}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{*}\mathbb{T}_{T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}}

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim}

where the fiber on the left is computed thanks to thanks to Corollary
4.2.22
(since

integrates well) and the fiber on the right is computed using connections on

and
Z(\rho^{*})
.

In general the fiber of a pullback in a stable category are equivalent if and only square on the right is a pullback:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{fib}(A\to B)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{fib}(C\to D)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces C}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces D}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim}

We can see that by considering the following diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{fib}(A\to B)\simeq\mathrm{fib}(C\to D)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces C}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 0}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces D}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim}

Then the left square is a pullback and the outer square is a pullback if and only if the fibers are equivalent. Then it is a general property of the pullback in a stable category that if the outer square and the left square are Cartesians then the right square is also Cartesian. ∎

Now we are going to see that similarly to the situation for group action, this notion of moment map is well behaved with respect to Lagrangian intersections. To do so we will need an analogue to the notion of symplectic reduction of a Lagrangian morphism (Definition
4.3.8
).

Definition 4.3.18
.

Consider a Lagrangian

4.3.3.
For groupoids

We will now give a definition of a moment map for actions of
Segal groupoids
and then see that “infinitesimal” moment maps from Section
4.3.2
are the “infinitesimal version” of the moment maps for Segal groupoids (see Theorem
4.3.30
).

The critical examples we want to recover are the moment maps for a group actions (Example
4.3.24
) and the dual of the anchor
T^{*}X\to L^{*}[n]
(Proposition
4.3.25
) of a Lie algebroid.

Remark 4.3.22
.

Recall that for any Segal groupoid
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
over
X
a derived stack, such that the cotangent complexes of each
\mathscr{G}^{n}
exists, then we can define the anchored linear stack:

In this degree of generality, we do not know if this is a Lie algebroid, but in order to mimic the role of

in the previous section, having just an anchored linear stack is enough.

The notion of moment map in this situation can be directly adapted from the infinitesimal case.

Theorem 4.3.28
.

Let
\mu:Y\to L^{*}[n]
be a
n
-shifted moment map and
L_{1}\to Y
and
L_{2}\to Y
Lagrangian morphisms with symplectic reductions. Then the moment map
\mu
induces a moment map:

\mu_{-1}:L_{1}\times_{Y}L_{2}\to L^{*}[n-1]

Moreover, there is a natural equivalence:

{\left(L_{1}\times_{Y}L_{2}\right)}_{\mathrm{red}}\simeq{(L_{1})}_{\mathrm{red}}\times_{{L}_{\mathrm{red}}}{(L_{2})}_{\mathrm{red}}

Proof.

–

We need an action of
\mathscr{L}
on
Z(\mu_{-1})
. We have:

\begin{split}Z(\mu_{-1})\simeq&(L_{1}\times_{Y}L_{2})\times_{(X\times_{L^{*}[n]}X)}(X\times_{X}X)\\
\simeq&L_{1}\times_{Z(\mu)}L_{2}\end{split}

Since
L_{1}
,
L_{2}
and
Y
all have an action of
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
, by pullback of actions of groupoids (Proposition
4.1.19
). We get a pullback action of
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
on
Z(\mu_{-1})
.

–

We have thanks to Proposition
4.1.19
:

\begin{split}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu_{-1})}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu_{-1})}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu_{-1})}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu_{-1})}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\simeq&\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{1}\times_{Z(\mu)}L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{1}\times_{Z(\mu)}L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{1}\times_{Z(\mu)}L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{1}\times_{Z(\mu)}L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\\
\simeq&\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.8375pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.3125pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\\
\simeq&{(L_{1})}_{\mathrm{red}}\times_{{Y}_{\mathrm{red}}}{(L_{2})}_{\mathrm{red}}\end{split}

This is a derived intersection of Lagrangians by assumption therefore it is
(n-1)
-shifted symplectic.

Corollary 4.3.29
.

Let
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
be a smooth Segal groupoid over
X
. The Lagrangian maps
s_{0},df:X\to T^{*}X
have symplectic reductions given by:

s_{0},d\left[f\right]:\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\to T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]

as soon as
f
is
\mathscr{G}
-invariant. Using Proposition
4.3.25
and Theorem
4.3.28
, we get a
(-1)
-shifted moment map
\mathbf{Crit}(f)\to L^{*}[-1]
whose symplectic reduction is exactly the
\mathscr{G}
-equivariant derived critical locus,
\mathbf{Crit}(\left[f\right])
.

Proof.

Since
f
is equivariant,
df
factors through
Z(\mu)
(idem for
s_{0}
) and we have the diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z(\mu)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\star}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T^{*}X}

The square is clearly a pullback from Lemma
4.1.18
and the maps:

\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\to T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]

are either
d\left[f\right]
or the zero section (and therefore they are Lagrangian).

Therefore
df
and
s_{0}
both have a symplectic reduction.

We have seen in Proposition
4.3.25
that
T^{*}X\to L^{*}
is a moment map with symplectic reduction
T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]
and using Theorem
4.3.28
, we get a
(-1)
-shifted moment map:

\mu_{-1}:\mathbf{Crit}(f)\to L^{*}[-1]

whose symplectic reduction is:

{\mathbf{Crit}(f)}_{\mathrm{red}}\simeq\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\times_{T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]=:\mathbf{Crit}(\left[f\right])

∎

Following the idea of Section
4.2.1
where we want to explain that infinitesimal quotients by Lie algebroids are formal completions along the projections to the quotients by groupoids. Similarly, we have that infinitesimal symplectic reductions are formal completions of symplectic reductions and more generally all the constructions of Section
4.3.2
are “infinitesimal versions” of the constructions of the current section.

Theorem 4.3.30
.

Let
\mathscr{L}
be a Lie algebroid over
X
, an affine stack satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
. We assume that
\mathscr{L}
integrates well and we pick
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
a good integration of
\mathscr{L}
(see Definition
4.2.13
).
Take
\mu:Y\to L^{*}[n]
a
n
-shifted moment map for
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
and
L_{i}\to X
(
i=1..2
) Lagrangian morphisms with symplectic reduction for
\mathscr{G}
such that
Y
,
L_{i}
and
Z(\mu)
are all affine of almost finite presentation. Then we have the following:

(1)

\mu
has a canonical infinitesimal moment map structure with symplectic reduction given by the weak infinitesimal quotient obtained as the formal completion:

\widetilde{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}:=\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}

(2)

The infinitesimal symplectic reductions of
L_{i}
(for
i=1..2
) are given by the weak infinitesimal quotients obtained as the formal completions of the symplectic reductions of
L_{i}
:

\widetilde{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}:=\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}

(3)

The infinitesimal shifted moment map obtained by Lagrangian intersection (Theorem
4.3.20
):

\mu_{-1}:L_{1}\times_{Y}L_{2}\to L^{*}[n-1]

is the moment map obtained by the first construction applied to shifted moment map obtained via Lagrangian intersection for groupoids (Theorem
4.3.28
).

Therefore, the infinitesimal symplectic reduction of the derived intersection is the formal completion of the projection to the symplectic reduction of the derived intersection.

Lemma 4.3.31
.

Take
Z
and
Y
two affine stacks of almost finite presentation.
Let
\mathscr{G}
be a groupoid over
Z
and take a Lagrangian correspondence:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y}

then there is a canonical Lagrangian correspondence:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widehat{X_{Z}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y}

Proof.

Recall from Lemma
1.3.20
that there is a factorization:

Z\to\widehat{X_{Z}}\to X

where the first map is a formal thickening and the last map is formally étale. We get the diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widehat{X_{Z}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i}

Pulling back the symplectic structure along
i
gives again a symplectic structure because
i
is formally étale. Therefore the isotropic correspondence can be chosen to be the same. Then since the non-degeneracy condition only depends on the tangent and cotangent complexes,
i
being formally étale implies that the isotropic correspondence we obtained is also non-degenerate.
∎

Proof of Theorem
4.3.30
.

\simeq&\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}\end{split}

Therefore the upper square is also a pullback and
\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{Z(\mu)}}
is both a weak infinitesimal quotient and the symplectic reduction for the infinitesimal moment map thanks to Lemma
4.3.31
.

(2)

We have the commutative diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{i}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z(\mu)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{L_{i}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{Z(\mu)}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}

where all squares are pullback squares (for the same reason as in the proof of (1)). Moreover, it is not hard to see (using again that the lower vertical maps are formally étale, as in the proof of Lemma
4.3.31
) that the maps:

\widetilde{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]}:=\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{L_{i}}}\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]

have Lagrangian structures canonically determined by the Lagrangian structures on

\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\to\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]

Moreover,
\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{L_{i}}}
is a weak infinitesimal quotient for exactly the same reason than
\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{Z(\mu)}}
in the proof of (1).
This gives
L_{i}
the structure of an infinitesimal Lagrangian symplectic reduction with reduction given by
\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{i}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{L_{i}}}
.

(3)

Consider the diagram where all squares are pullbacks:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z(\mu)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{L_{1}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{Z(\mu)}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{L_{2}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}

The idea is that taking the fiber along the horizontal morphisms produces the Lagrangian intersections we are looking for, and the formal completion of the pullback morphisms is the pullback of the formal completions (Corollary
1.3.13
).

More precisely, the moment map structure on:

\mu_{-1}:Z(\mu_{-1})\simeq L_{1}\times_{Z(\mu)}L_{2}\to L^{*}[-1]\simeq X\times_{L^{*}}X

is given by the pullback action (Proposition
4.1.19
) and gives us a Lagrangian correspondence:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z(\mu_{-1})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu_{-1})}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu_{-1})}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu_{-1})}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu_{-1})}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{1}\times_{Y}L_{2}}

with:

\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu_{-1})}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.75pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu_{-1})}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu_{-1})}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu_{-1})}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\simeq\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.8375pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.3125pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]

Then the infinitesimal moment map induced by first construction is given by the same underlying map
\mu_{-1}
, the same fiber of the moment map,
Z(\mu_{-1})
, and we only need to find the weak infinitesimal quotient. It is given by the formal completion which can be computed as (again thanks to Corollary
1.3.13
):

\begin{split}\widehat{\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.8375pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.3125pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\right)_{Z(\mu_{-1})}}\simeq&\widehat{\left(\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\times_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.8375pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.3125pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\right)_{L_{1}\times_{Z(\mu)}L_{2}}}\\
\simeq&\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{1}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{L_{1}}}\times_{\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\displaystyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.625pt}{$\textstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.8375pt}{$\scriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.3125pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{Z(\mu)}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{Z(\mu)}}}\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{L_{2}}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{L_{2}}}\end{split}

But the last term is exactly the weak infinitesimal quotient obtained by Lagrangian intersection of the infinitesimal moment maps by the infinitesimal Lagrangian reductions described before.

∎

To compute the particular example of this construction applied to the dual of the anchor map
T^{*}X\to L^{*}
(with respect to a groupoid action), we use the following proposition:

Proposition 4.3.32
.

Let
X
be an affine stack satisfying Assumptions
3.2.2
. Take
\mathscr{L}
a Lie algebroid over
X
that integrates well to a good groupoid
\mathscr{G}
. Then there is an equivalence:

T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]\simeq\widehat{\left(T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\right)_{Z(\mu)}}

Proof.

We consider the following morphism:

Then we have a commutative diagram such that all squares are pullbacks:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z(\mu)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha^{*}T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\simeq\widehat{\left(T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\right)_{Z(\mu)}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]\simeq\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}

The outer square is clearly a pullback square since there is an equivalence:

p^{*}\mathbb{L}_{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.67416pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.19583pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]}\simeq\mathbb{L}_{X}\oplus^{\rho^{*}}\mathscr{L}^{\vee}[-1]

For the lower square,
\alpha^{*}T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]
is the pullback by definition.

From Corollary
4.2.7
, since
\mathscr{L}
integrates well, we get the equivalence:

\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]\simeq\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}

Finally using Corollary
1.3.13
this shows that
\widehat{\left(T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\right)_{Z(\mu)}}
is also the pullback of the lower square.

Using Lemma
1.3.20
, the map:

\widehat{\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]_{X}}\overset{\alpha}{\to}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]

is formally étale. Therefore there is an equivalence:

\alpha^{*}T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]\overset{\sim}{\to}T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]

∎

In particular if
\mathscr{L}
integrates well to
\mathscr{G}^{\bullet}
, then this proposition shows that
T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]
is canonically symplectic if and only if
T^{*}\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{G}}$}}}\right]
is also canonically symplectic.

5.
Derived Perspective of the BV Complex

The classical BV construction is a mean to build an algebra of classical observables associated with a space of fields
X
together with an action functional
f
taking into account some symmetries of the system. There are two different approaches to construct these algebras:

Construction 5.0.1
.

The idea for the first construction is given by the following two steps:

(1)

First, take
S
a “space of solutions” to the Euler–Lagrange equation. In our setting it amounts to solving
df=0
.

(2)

Then take a “infinitesimal quotient” of
S
by a Lie algebroid of “maximal symmetries” so that this infinitesimal quotient is
(-1)
-shifted symplectic.

This is the approach corresponding to the construction in
[
FK14
]
which we will discuss in more details in Construction
5.1.1
.

Construction 5.0.2
.

The second approach takes these operations in reverse:

(1)

First take a Lie algebroid “of symmetries” on
X
. In particular,
f
must be equivariant with respect to the infinitesimal action of this algebroid and we get a map
117
117

117

Or rather “being” equivariant is the data of such a map (see Definition
4.2.24
).
:

\left[f\right]:\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]\to\mathbb{A}_{k}^{1}

(2)

We take the derived critical locus of the equivariant map viewed as the (derived) space of solutions of the Euler–Lagrange equations.

This is similar to the approach of
[
CG21
]
which is going to be studied in more details in Section
5.3.3
(in a restricted setting).

The goal of this section is to provide a setting fitting and generalizing both constructions. We will argue that both constructions are intances of a notion of “generalized derived symplectic reduction” of the derived critical locus by a choice of given infinitesimal symmetries.

Moreover, we will discuss a variation of this construction for symmetries which are not infinitesimal but given by
Segal groupoids
of symmetries.

Finally, we show in Section
5.3
that any groupoid or Lie algebroid of “off-shell symmetries” induces a canonical BV construction by symplectic reduction of a canonical
(-1)
-shifted moment map on the derived critical locus.

5.1.
BV as a Generalized Derived Symplectic Reduction

In this section, we start in Section
5.1.1
by explaining in more details Constructions
5.0.1
and
5.0.2
and show that they are both instances of a notion of “generalized symplectic reduction” of the derived critical locus (see Section
5.1.2
).

In Section
5.2.1
we try to explain to what extent this general construction still resembles the usual BV constructions. We will in particular see that we get the same kind of algebras (Proposition
5.2.3
). However, in general we cannot strictify the
(-1)
-shifted symplectic structure as it may admit “higher” terms (Theorem
5.2.8
).

5.1.1.
Context and construction for infinitesimal actions

Through all of Section
5
, we will take
X=\mathbf{Spec}(A)
a smooth affine algebraic variety
118
118

118

In particular,
X
satisfies Assumptions
3.2.2
and a map
f:X\to\mathbb{A}_{k}^{1}
. We start by describing the BV algebra as constructed in
[
FK14
]
:

Construction 5.1.1
.

(1)

The first step is to pick a resolution of the strict critical locus. We take a semi-free resolution called the

) of the strict critical locus of a function

\KT(f):=\left(\Sym_{A}\left(\mathbb{T}_{A}[1]\oplus\mathscr{L}_{\KT}[2]\right),\delta_{\KT}\right)

where
\mathscr{L}_{\KT}
is projective concentrated in non-positive degrees.
\mathscr{L}_{\KT}
and

are chosen so that the cohomology of this complex is concentrated in degree

and giving in degree
0

{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{A}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.75pt}{$\displaystyle{\langle df.X,X\in\mathbb{T}_{A}\rangle}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{A}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.75pt}{$\textstyle{\langle df.X,X\in\mathbb{T}_{A}\rangle}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{A}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.75pt}{$\scriptstyle{\langle df.X,X\in\mathbb{T}_{A}\rangle}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{A}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.75pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\langle df.X,X\in\mathbb{T}_{A}\rangle}$}}}

(2)

From here we consider the following graded algebra (with no differential):

\BV_{\FK}^{\sharp}=\Sym_{A}\left(\mathbb{T}_{A}[1]\oplus\mathscr{L}_{\KT}[2]\oplus\widehat{\mathscr{L}_{\KT}^{\vee}[-1]}\right)

where the symbol
\widehat{-}
means that we take the completion along the Chevalley–Eilenberg terms,
\mathscr{L}_{\KT}^{\vee}[-1]
(see Notation

).

(3)

This graded algebra is
(-1)
-shifted symplectic together with the canonical
119
119

119

Canonical is the sens that it is induced by the canonical symplectic structure on
\mathbf{Crit}(f)
(induced by the Poisson pairing between
B
and
\mathbb{T}_{B}[1]
) and the canonical pairing between
\mathscr{L}_{\KT}[2]
and
\mathscr{L}_{\KT}^{\vee}[-1]
. This is the strict structure from Definition
5.2.6
symplectic structure.

(4)

By an inductive procedure, we can construct a BV charge (
[
FK14
, Theorem 4.5]
),
Q\in(\BV_{\FK}^{\sharp})_{0}
satisfying the
Classical Master Equation
:

\{Q,Q\}=0

This can be equivalently phrased as finding a differential
\delta_{\FK}
on
\BV_{\FK}^{\sharp}
that is Hamiltonian,
\delta_{\FK}=\{Q,-\}
. This differential also respects the filtration given by the symmetric power in
\mathscr{L}^{\vee}[-1]
. Moreover, this differential restricts to the Koszul–Tate differential defining a map,
\BV_{\FK}\to\KT(f)
, of algebras. We get the full BV algebra:

\BV_{\FK}:=\left(\BV_{\FK}^{\sharp},\{-,-\},Q\right)

We will try to rephrase this construction as follows:

–

Start by taking the derived critical locus whose algebra of functions
120
120

120

This is also called the Koszul complex, to which we then add the Tate terms,
\mathscr{L}_{\KT}
to produce the Koszul–Tate resolution.
is
\Sym_{A}\mathbb{T}_{A}[1]
with differential
\iota_{df}
(thanks to
1.2.21
). Then taking the Koszul–Tate resolution amounts to adding “anti-ghost fields” (see Remark
1.2.23
) generating
\mathscr{L}_{\KT}[2]
that will kill the higher cohomology of the derived critical locus, in other words, kill the symmetries of
f
. Note that there is a natural map:

\iKT(f)\to\mathbf{Crit}(f)

–

We can pullback the sympletic form of the derived critical locus to a pre-symplectic form on
\iKT(f)
and the “kernel” of this pre-symplectic form is essentially given by
\mathscr{L}_{\KT}
, in other words the “anti-ghost fields generating the symmetries”.

–

We add “ghost fields” dual to the anti-ghost fields to kill this kernel, and we get a symplectic structure. Adding these ghost fields amounts to taking the
Chevalley–Eilenberg algebra
of a
\mathscr{L}_{\infty}
-algebroid of maximal symmetries over the Koszul–Tate resolution.

It also turns out that the use of
\iKT(f)
is to restrictive if we want to recover Construction
5.0.2
. Indeed, in most case, this second construction cannot recover a full resolution of the strict critical locus. This construction is given by:

Construction 5.1.2
.

(1)

Start with a Lie algebroid (or

-algebroid)
\mathscr{L}
over
X
of “infinitesimal symmetries”, i.e. such that

is
\mathscr{L}
-equivariant, and we have a map:

\left[f\right]:\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{X}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]\to\mathbb{A}^{1}

(2)

Take the derived critical locus
\mathbf{Crit}(\left[f\right])
who is naturally
(-1)
-shifted symplectic.

Heuristically
121
121

121

As we have seen in Sections
3
and
4
, this heuristic is not really clear. In practice the Chevalley–Eilenberg algebra is use as a model for derived invariant although its relationship to infinitesimal quotient is not clear.
, the first step amounts to considering the Chevalley–Eilenberg algebra of the Lie algebroid of symmetry we start with (which amounts to first add the ghost fields).

Then taking the derived critical locus amounts to adding the anti-fields and anti-ghost fields. Let us have an incorrect motivating discussion. We somehow look at the derived critical locus of a functional on the Chevalley–Eilenberg algebra. We would think that its algebra of functions would be like:

\Sym_{\mathrm{CE}(\mathscr{L})}\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{CE}(\mathscr{L})}[1]\simeq\Sym_{A}\left(\mathbb{T}_{A}[1]\oplus\mathscr{L}[2]\oplus\mathscr{L}^{\vee}[-1]\right)

and we would recover the general shape of the BV algebra from

]
. However, the differential on this algebra would be the contraction
\iota_{d\left[f\right]}
and linearization of the Chevalley–Eilenberg differential which
cannot

(in particular the terms increasing the symmetric power cannot appear).

The correct way to view the relation between the second and first constructions is discussed in Sections

,
5.3.3
and
5.3.4
. However, this discussion motivates a generalization of Construction

where we add anti-ghost fields, but not necessarily making it a resolution. This procedure of adding anti-ghost fields corresponds to choosing an
almost derived critical locus
(Definition

5.1.2.
Generalized BV construction

The idea that we had so far boils done to taking an almost derived critical locus
S\hookrightarrow\mathbf{Crit}(f)
and then take its quotient to make it
(-1)
-shifted symplectic. This is the general idea behind
symplectic reduction
, and we will describe the BV construction in those terms. This motivates, by analogy with Definition
4.3.12

Convention 5.1.5
.

Note that the notion of “infinitesimal quotient” in the previous definition is unclear. We have the following possible notion of infinitesimal quotient:

(1)

The first naive notion that mimics Construction
5.1.1
is to consider a perfect
\mathscr{L}_{\infty}
-algebroid
\mathscr{L}
on
S
and define:

{Y}_{\mathrm{red}}:=\mathbf{Spec}(\mathrm{CE}(\mathscr{L}))

However, the natural projection
S\to{Y}_{\mathrm{red}}
needs not be a formal thickening, therefore the adjective “infinitesimal” is not really fitting.

(2)

We can could consider the formal completion of the previous example:

{Y}_{\mathrm{red}}:=\widehat{\mathbf{Spec}(\mathrm{CE}(\mathscr{L}))_{S}}

From Lemma
4.3.31
, if
\mathbf{Spec}(\mathrm{CE}(\mathscr{L}))
is part of a Lagrangian correspondence, then so is its formal completion. Moreover, this formal completion is a formal thickening of
S
.

(3)

In a similar idea, we can also consider infinitesimal quotients of the form:

{Y}_{\mathrm{red}}:=\underline{\mathbf{Spf}_{A}(\mathrm{CE}(\mathscr{L}))}

(4)

In Section
3.2.1
, we define the notion of infinitesimal quotient of a Lie algebroid. If
S
satisfies Assumptions
3.2.2
, we can define:

{Y}_{\mathrm{red}}:=\underline{\MC_{\mathscr{L}}}\simeq\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{S}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\displaystyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{S}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-3.41666pt}{$\textstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{S}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-2.39166pt}{$\scriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}{\raisebox{1.70833pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{S}$}\mkern-5.0mu\diagup\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{-1.6994pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle{\mathscr{L}}$}}}\right]

For example,
S
satisfies Assumptions
3.2.2
if
S=\iKT(f)
, but
S
will
not
satisfy these Assumptions in the context of Construction
5.1.2
.

(5)

S
admits a map
S\to X
where
X
satisfies Assumptions
3.2.2
and
\mathscr{L}
is a Lie algebroid on
X
. We can consider the weak infinitesimal quotients (Definition
4.2.19
) associated to
\mathscr{L}
.

We will typically use this notion of weak infinitesimal quotient in the situation where we have “off-shell symmetries” (Definition
5.1.14
).

Claim 5.1.6
.

The different notions of infinitesimal quotients given in Definition
5.1.5
are related as follows:

–

Any infinitesimal quotient in the sens of (1) induces an infinitesimal quotient in the sens of (2) by formal completion. A generalized symplectic reduction for (1) induces a generalized symplectic reduction for (2). Therefore the second definition is strictly better as it is a formal thickening.

–

We have a natural morphism:

\underline{\mathbf{Spf}_{A}(\mathrm{CE}(\mathscr{L}))}_{\mathrm{pre}}\to\widehat{\mathbf{Spec}(\mathrm{CE}(\mathscr{L}))_{S}}

–

If
S
satisfies Assumptions
3.2.2
, then any Lie algebroid over
S
acts on
S
along the identity
S\to S
. Then the infinitesimal quotient of
S
is a weak infinitesimal quotient. Therefore infinitesimal quotients in the sens of (4) are weak infinitesimal quotients in the sens of (5).

We can observe that there are essentially two kinds of infinitesimal quotients. The ones based on the Chevalley–Eilenberg algebra, which are useful to relate these quotient with BV-like algebras as we described before.

The other ones are infinitesimal quotient as discussed in Sections
3
and
4
which we claim to be a more geometric approach to infinitesimal quotients.

We believe that in order to reconcile the two pictures, we need to remember the
graded mixed
structure on the Chevalley–Eilenberg algebra (at least when the Lie algebroid is perfect). The correct notion of infinitesimal quotients and the tools to manipulate them still need to be improved on.

We have said multiple times in Section
4.3
that the equivariant derived critical locus
\mathbf{Crit}(\left[f\right])
is the symplectic reduction of the derived critical locus. As
\mathbf{Crit}(\left[f\right])
is supposed to represent the BV-construction (following Construction
5.0.2
). In particular
\mathrm{Crit}(f)
itself should be viewed as the simplest derived critical locus. Then we argue that adding ghosts and anti-ghosts fields geometrically corresponds to taking a generalized symplectic reduction, motivating the following definitions:

Definition 5.1.7
.

A
BV construction for
f
is the structure of generalized derived symplectic reduction on
S
, an almost derived critical locus, along the map:

S\to\mathbf{Crit}(f)

Definition 5.1.8
.

An
infinitesimal BV construction for
f
is the structure of generalized infinitesimal derived symplectic reduction on
S
, an almost derived critical locus of almost finite presentation, along the map:

S\to\mathbf{Crit}(f)

Again, this definition depends on the choice of a notion of infinitesimal quotient as in Definition
5.1.5
.

Remark 5.1.9
.

Given an almost derived critical locus
S
on
f
, the existence of a BV construction (infinitesimal or not) for that
S
is not obvious. A large class of examples of BV constructions will be given in Section
5.3
.

Given an almost derived critical locus
S
on
f
and assuming that it admits a generalized symplectic reduction (infinitesimal or not) there is a priori no reason to have a unique such reduction associated to
S
and
f
. There is in fact a full topological space of such structures which needs not be contractible or even connected.

Remark 5.1.10
.

It is worth noticing that any two BV constructions are related by a Lagrangian correspondence:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces S_{1}\times_{\mathbf{Crit}(f)}S_{2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces S_{1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces S_{2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\BV_{1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Crit}(f)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\BV_{2}}

Viewed those Lagrangians as admissible morphisms, this defines a neither full or faithful sub-category of
\mathrm{Lag}_{1}(\star)_{/\mathrm{Crit}(f)}
.

Remark 5.1.11
.

Our abstract definition of BV construction (infinitesimal or not) might be “too general” a priori and have nothing to do with what a BV algebra usually “looks like”. Although our objects are in fact much more general than the classical construction mainly due to the added flexibility of homotopy structures, we will see argue in Section
5.2.1
that our construction still “looks like” the classical BV construction.

Remark 5.1.12
.

The construction from
[
FK14
]
and
[
CG21
]
are both infinitesimal BV constructions. Some ideas behind global (non-infinitesimal) BV construction for group actions are discussed in
[
BSS21
]
. Our definition however works in a more general context including Segal groupoid actions.

5.1.3.
Off-shell symmetries

In this Section, we are going to discuss BV constructions that arise from an action (infinitesimal or not) on
X
such that
f
is equivariant with respect to that action.

Definition 5.1.14
.

We say that an action on an almost derived critical locus
S
is an action by
off-shell
symmetries if:

–

It is
off-shell
, that is, it comes from an action (in the sens of
4.1.15
) of a groupoid
\mathscr{G}
over
X
on
\pi_{S}:S\to X
.

–

f
is
\mathscr{G}
-equivariant in the sens of Definition
4.1.12
.

Definition 5.1.15
.

Let
S
be an almost derived critical locus of almost finite presentation. Then an infinitesimal quotient
{Y}_{\mathrm{red}}
is a weak infinitesimal quotient by
off-shell
symmetries if:

–

There is an algebroid
\mathscr{L}
on
X
such that
f
is
\mathscr{L}
-equivariant (Definition
4.2.24
).

–

{Y}_{\mathrm{red}}
is a weak infinitesimal quotient of
S
along
S\to X
.

If
S
satisfies Assumptions
3.2.2
, we instead require that the quotient comes from an infinitesimal action of
\mathscr{L}
on
S\to X
.

Definition 5.1.16
.

An
off-shell (infinitesimal) BV construction
is a (infinitesimal) BV construction whose symplectic reduction is obtained either by:

–

a quotient of
S
by a groupoid of off-shell symmetries.

–

or a weak infinitesimal quotient coming from an algebroid of infinitesimal off-shell symmetries.

Remark 5.1.17
.

Not only there are plenty of examples of such off-shell symmetries, but we will see in Sections
5.3.3
and
5.3.4
that for any Lie algebroid of off-shell symmetries (infinitesimal or not), we can construct an (infinitesimal or not) BV construction essentially given by the

.

defines a weak infinitesimal quotient.

,
